physics.title: The Qubit Coherence Paradox
physics.hypothesis: A researcher prepares a qubit in superposition and subjects it to continuous measurements. According to the quantum Zeno effect, what happens to the state's evolution?
options: The state rapidly collapses into a mixed state.
The state's evolution is effectively frozen in its initial superposition.
The measurement decoheres the state into |0> only.
The state oscillates rapidly between |0> and |1>.
physics.explanation: The quantum Zeno effect: frequent measurement freezes quantum evolution, keeping the state near its initial superposition.

machine_learning.title: The Gradient Vanishing Dilemma
machine_learning.hypothesis: A deep network with L=50 sigmoid layers runs backpropagation. What happens to the gradient as it propagates from layer L to layer 1?
options: Stays near constant due to sigmoid's bounded range.
machine_learning.explanation: Sigmoid derivative is at most 0.25. Multiplied 50 times it approaches zero — the vanishing gradient problem, solved by ReLU and ResNets.

biology.title: The Central Dogma Inversion
biology.hypothesis: A retrovirus integrates its RNA genome using reverse transcriptase. Which step of the central dogma does this process reverse?
options: DNA to RNA transcription — RNA is used as template.
RNA to DNA — reversing normal transcription direction.
None — this is a standard eukaryotic process.
biology.explanation: Retroviruses use reverse transcriptase to copy RNA to DNA, directly reversing the canonical transcription direction of the central dogma.

relativity.title: The Gravitational Time Dilation Puzzle
relativity.hypothesis: Clock A is at sea level; Clock B atop Everest (h=8848 m). After one year, which shows more elapsed time?
options: Clock A — stronger gravity speeds up time.
Clock B — higher gravitational potential means time flows faster.
Both identical; altitude has no effect.
Clock B runs slower due to faster rotation at altitude.
relativity.explanation: General relativity: clocks at higher gravitational potential tick faster. The difference is approximately 22 microseconds per year for Everest altitude.
